questions.explanation: Net investment of 4 added to 200 gives 204 million; the tempting error adds gross 15. Use net.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Interpret enforcement reform data
questions.stem: A board table shows investment rising after enforcement reform but GDP unchanged; what is a cautious reading?

options.text: Investment responded but broader growth effects may lag.
Enforcement has no effect on anything.
Investment data must be wrong.
GDP never follows investment.

questions.explanation: Investment can respond before aggregate output moves; the tempting overclaim dismisses the reform. Lags are normal.

questions.learningObjective: Compute risk-adjusted return
questions.stem: Gross return is 14 percent and risk premium is 3 percent; what is the risk-adjusted return?
questions.explanation: Subtracting the risk premium from gross gives 11 percent; the tempting error adds. Adjust down.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Identify an anti-corruption measure
questions.stem: Which measure best reduces corruption in transit procurement?

options.text: Secret negotiations with a single bidder.
Eliminating all documentation requirements.
Transparent, competitive bidding with oversight.
Paying officials bonuses tied to speed only.

questions.explanation: Transparency and competition limit rent extraction; the tempting view thinks speed bonuses help. Incentives must protect integrity.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain public capital maintenance
questions.stem: Explain why deferring maintenance on transit capital raises future costs.

answer.exemplar: Deferred maintenance accelerates deterioration, so later repairs cost more and service quality falls; spending a little now avoids large replacement costs.

questions.explanation: Delay accelerates decay and raises replacement costs; the tempting view saves money now. Lifecycle costs rise.
